records.name: Gillin Boat Club
records.summary: The boathouse at 2200 Kelly Drive, shared by two St. Joseph's rowing programs, which also hosts a city youth rowing program run with the Fairmount Park Commission. We could not confirm that the youth program is running now.
records.what_you_do: City youth can try rowing through the Fairmount Park Commission program that the club hosts. The club's own rowing teams are the two St. Joseph's programs.

first_step.how: Ask the Fairmount Park Commission whether its community rowing program for city youth is running this year. The boathouse is at 2200 Kelly Drive.
first_step.basis: The program is for city youth, but we found no current sign-up details.

records.notes: No club website is linked from the Schuylkill Navy members page, so no group page was read. Facts come from Wikipedia. The newest dated trace is a 2009 camp brochure cited in that article, so status is unknown.

records.name: Hines Rowing Center
records.summary: A rowing club based in Conshohocken, outside the city, with learn-to-row, high performance and masters programs.
records.what_you_do: The site links to an adult learn-to-row program that runs through Whitemarsh Boat Club.
records.notes: Out of area: the campus is in Conshohocken (Montgomery County) and the site lists no Philadelphia program. It is an associate member on the Schuylkill Navy members page. The Campus Calendar page returned 404, and the home page shows no dated items. Phone and email not found. Office address per the site: 18 Elizabeth St, West Conshohocken, PA 19428.

records.name: Malta Boat Club
records.summary: A rowing club on Boathouse Row, founded in 1860, with a boathouse on the Schuylkill and social rowing for members.
records.what_you_do: Members store boats and use the meeting rooms, the heated erg room and the weight room. Some race, volunteer, officiate or coach in Schuylkill Navy events, and others row socially.

first_step.how: Call the club at (215) 769-9030 and ask about joining. The site says membership is open to anyone interested in the sport.
first_step.basis: Membership is open to anyone interested, but the cost, age rules and joining steps were not on the site.

records.notes: The site has no dated news or events. The events page returned 404. Probably_active is set only because the site works and shows no dates. Cost and joining steps not found.

records.name: Penn AC Rowing Association
records.summary: The rowing arm of the Penn Athletic Club on Boathouse Row, with masters and high performance rowing, a summer camp for high school students, and Learn to Row classes open to the public.
records.what_you_do: Adults can take the public Learn to Row classes to try rowing. Members can row in the club's masters and racing groups.

first_step.how: Sign up for a public Learn to Row class through the club's site. The price and the sign-up steps were not on the home page.
first_step.basis: Learn to Row classes are open to the public, but the page does not say how to sign up or what they cost.

records.notes: The batch name was Penn Athletic Club. This record is its rowing association, and the athletic club itself was not checked. The site has no dated items, and the events page returned 404. The address and phone were not on the home page, and the Contact Us link returned no details to our fetch.

records.name: Pennsylvania Barge Club
records.summary: A rowing club at 4 Boathouse Row on the Schuylkill and a full member of the Schuylkill Navy. We could not read its own website, so its programs and joining steps are not confirmed.
records.notes: The club's website on the members page did not resolve when fetched (DNS not found), so the site may have moved. The address and history come from Wikipedia. The Pennsylvania Center for Adaptive Sport site also gives 4 Boathouse Row as its address, so one of the two sources may be out of date.

records.name: Pennsylvania Center for Adaptive Sport
records.summary: A nonprofit that runs sports, recreation and wellness programs for people with disabilities, from rowing and kayaking to yoga and skiing, plus youth camps and volunteer days.
records.what_you_do: People with disabilities can join listed programs such as rowing, cycling, climbing, yoga or pickleball. Volunteers help with the adaptive rowing program and with spring cleanups at the garden.

locations.label: Office on Boathouse Row
locations.address: 4 Boathouse Row, Kelly Drive, Philadelphia, PA 19130

first_step.how: Pick a program from the adult or youth list on the site, then use the contact page to ask about it. Registration steps are not on the home page.
first_step.basis: Programs are listed openly, but eligibility, cost and registration steps are not shown on the home page.

records.notes: The home page lists a Cinco de Mayo ride and a Garden Spring Cleanup with no years, so status is probably_active by the no-date rule. The events page returned 404. The eligibility link opens an external document that we did not open. Its 4 Boathouse Row address matches the number Wikipedia gives for Pennsylvania Barge Club.

records.name: Philadelphia City Rowing
records.summary: A rowing club and associate member of the Schuylkill Navy. We could not read its website, so its programs and joining steps are not confirmed.

records.name: Philadelphia Girls Rowing Club
records.summary: A Schuylkill Navy rowing club with an adult rowing program, a member area and a regatta page on its site.
records.what_you_do: Adults can take the club's rowing program. New people start from the How To Join page, which we could not read.

first_step.how: Open the How To Join page on the club's website.
first_step.basis: A How To Join page exists, but the steps and cost were not visible to us.

records.notes: The .com address redirects (301) to the .org site, and the .org site was used. The site has no dated items, so probably_active is set only because the site works. Location, phone and email not on the page. The name says girls, but the page does not state age or gender rules.

records.name: Sedgeley Club
records.summary: A women's social club on Boathouse Row in a historic clubhouse, known for lunches, teas and dinners, with a history of rowing, cycling, canoeing and walking.
records.what_you_do: Members take part in club lunches, teas, dinners and membership events, and guests are welcome at some of them. The clubhouse also rents its rooms for lectures, meetings and other events.

first_step.how: Use the Contact Membership page on the club's site to ask about joining and about upcoming membership events.
first_step.basis: It is a membership club, and the site does not show cost or joining steps.

records.notes: No dated events or news. The events page has no dated items either. The only years on the site are a 2023 copyright footer and a 125th anniversary caption, which are not sign-of-life dates. Phone recorded as published; its 610 area code is not a Philadelphia code.

records.name: Undine Barge Club
records.summary: A Boathouse Row rowing club founded in 1856, with team rowing, a summer program for rowers under 23 and a masters program.
records.what_you_do: Members use the boathouse and the club's equipment, row with team, summer and masters groups, and attend club dinners. New people start on the Becoming a Member page.

first_step.how: Read the Becoming a Member page on the club's site, or call (215) 765-9244 to ask how membership works.
first_step.basis: Membership is the way in, and the steps and costs were not on the page we read.

records.notes: The front page features a Saturday morning practice with no date. The news page returned 404. No dated items were found, so probably_active is set by the no-date rule.

records.name: University Barge Club
records.summary: A Boathouse Row rowing club founded in 1854, with a recreational program for adults who want fitness and social rowing, and a masters team that races locally.
records.what_you_do: Adults can join the recreational program and row at their own pace. The masters team trains together and races in local regattas.

first_step.how: Use the Contact page on the club's site to ask about the recreational program.
first_step.basis: The site describes the programs but not how to join, the cost or the age rules.

records.notes: The newest dated item on the site is 1987, a Boathouse Row landmark note, which is not a sign of life for the club. No news or events were found, and the news page returned 404. The Contact page was not opened. Status is probably_active by the no-date rule.

records.name: Vesper Boat Club
records.summary: A Boathouse Row rowing club with a post-college racing team, a masters racing program and a summer camp for rowers under 23.
records.what_you_do: Post-collegiate rowers train and race year round on the racing team. Masters rowers train and race at local and regional regattas. Athletes under 23 can join a three-month summer program.

first_step.how: Use the inquiry form on the Contact page to ask about the U23 summer program or masters racing.
first_step.basis: The club runs competitive programs, and its site shows no cost, beginner program or joining steps for new members.

records.notes: Newest dated item: a news post dated October 5, 2026, about a regatta result. The post's own address was not captured, so sign_of_life_url is the home page, where the post is listed. Phone and email not found.

records.name: Whitemarsh Boat Club
records.summary: A rowing club on the upper Schuylkill with learn-to-row and erg classes, masters rowing, youth camps and a program for breast cancer survivors.
records.what_you_do: Adults can take Learn to Row or Learn to Erg classes, join a masters club row or race team, or attend youth camps.
records.notes: Out of area: the physical address is in Conshohocken (Montgomery County), and the club serves the wider Delaware Valley. It is an associate member on the Schuylkill Navy members page. Newest dated item: a save-the-date post about the national Learn to Row Day, dated June 6, 2026. It shares a campus address with Hines Rowing Center. No phone or email on the contact page.

records.name: Second Street Irish Society
records.summary: An Irish society we know from a parade listing. We could not find its own public page, so what it does and how to join are not confirmed.
records.notes: No website of its own was found. The seed source, phillyparade.com, is the St. Patrick's Day Parade site, and it does not mention this society. Its listed contact is the parade association's, so it was not recorded as this club's contact. Web searches were used up on other records, so no name search was run for this group.

records.name: Sew What?! Donatucci Evening Sewcial
records.summary: An in-person get together at the Thomas F. Donatucci, Sr. Library for people who knit, crochet, sew, embroider, quilt or felt.
records.what_you_do: Bring your own project or start one from the library's supplies, share what you are making, and learn from other makers.

schedule.text: Tuesdays 4 to 6 pm (Evening Sewcial). A Friday 2 to 4 pm session (Afternoon Sewcial) is listed too.

first_step.how: Go to the Tuesday 4 to 6 pm session at the Donatucci branch, 1935 West Shunk Street, and bring a project or start one there. Call 215-685-1755 to confirm the next session.
first_step.basis: The listing says newcomers and experienced makers are both welcome and describes a session anyone can attend.

records.notes: Evidence comes from a web search that listed several Sew What sessions, including a Tuesday evening and a Friday afternoon series. The direct fetch of the cited event page returned 404, and the calendar index returned 403, so the July 28, 2026 date and session times are not verified on the page. Recheck before relying on them. Cost is not stated. Library tags on the listing include seniors, LGBTQ and bilingual programs.

records.name: Bachelors Barge Club
records.summary: A Boathouse Row rowing club for experienced and amateur rowers, offering group and individual coaching and winter training.
records.what_you_do: Rowers can take group or individual coaching, race, and train through the winter.
records.notes: Found on the Schuylkill Navy members page, not in this batch, so no batch lead id. The contact block shows template placeholder text (a sample street address, a 555 phone number and a placeholder email), so no contact details are recorded. The membership and pricing pages are linked but were not read. No dated items on the site.

records.name: Crescent Boat Club
records.summary: A member-run rowing club at 5 Kelly Drive on Boathouse Row, founded in 1867, that welcomes people with no rowing experience and offers summer coaching at every level.
records.what_you_do: Newcomers can start with an inquiry and take summer coaching from novice to sculling development. The club also has junior, under-23 and masters crews. Youth rowers apply through RegattaCentral.

first_step.how: Send an inquiry through the form on the Membership page. The page lists membership categories.
first_step.basis: The club says newcomers can join with no rowing experience and explains how to start by inquiry.

records.notes: Found on the Schuylkill Navy members page, not in this batch, so no batch lead id. Newest dated item: a post titled 2025 Summer Rowing Programs, dated May 2025 from its URL path, with no day shown. Dues amounts not found. The site has no published phone or email, only forms. For emergencies the site asks callers to give 842 Kelly Drive, not 5 Kelly Drive.

records.name: Fairmount Rowing Association
records.summary: A rowing club founded in 1877 at 2 Boathouse Row and known for masters rowing, with a small juniors program, a summer program and a masters regatta.
records.what_you_do: Adult masters rowers train and race with the club. The club also runs a small juniors program and a summer rowing program.

first_step.how: Open the Membership page on the club's site to see how to join. The summer rowing program has its own information page.
first_step.basis: A Membership page exists, but the cost, age rules and joining steps were not on the page we read.

The news items are labeled 2026 with no month (one about the Quaker City regatta, one about the 2026 summer program), so status is active on a year-only date. Phone not found. The Members Only section and its rules were not visible to us.

records.summary: A rowing center in Conshohocken, Montgomery County, with adult classes, youth summer camps and a sculling program for under-23 and senior rowers.
records.notes: Out of area: the center is in Conshohocken, and the site does not describe Philadelphia residents or a Philadelphia location. Found on the Schuylkill Navy members page, not in this batch, so no batch lead id. The site has no dated items. Joining steps and costs not found.

notes: Batch had 15 items; all 15 have records. Four more Schuylkill Navy clubs that have their own websites (Bachelors Barge, Crescent, Fairmount, Conshohocken Rowing Center) were found on the members page and checked; they are written as records with lead_ids empty, since they are not in this batch, so the orchestrator should dedupe them against other agents' output. College Boat Club has no website on the members page and is in leads_only. Verdicts: 16 publish, 3 out_of_area (Hines, Whitemarsh, Conshohocken Rowing Center, all in Conshohocken). Pennsylvania Barge Club and Philadelphia City Rowing have no readable site, so both are low confidence. The Sew What record rests on a web search snippet (its event page returned 404 on direct fetch), so it is low confidence. Searches: all 3 used (Gillin, Pennsylvania Barge Club, Sew What); none left for Second Street Irish Society. Fetches: 30 of 60. Address conflict to resolve: 4 Boathouse Row is given both for Pennsylvania Center for Adaptive Sport and for Pennsylvania Barge Club (Wikipedia).
